 Pembroke Pines DMV employee faces 360 felony counts in driver license fraud case 
 According to authorities, Lynette Sitt Williams was a driver's license examiner who issued licenses despite applicants having to re-take the driving exam. 
 By Ari Odzer and NBC6 • 
 Published November 17, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 17, 2026 at 7:12 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 A Pembroke Pines DMV employee is facing hundreds of felony counts in a drivers license fraud scheme. NBC6’s Ari Odzer reports
 Another employee with the Department of Motor Vehicles has been accused in a driver's license fraud scheme and faces hundreds of charges, authorities said.
 Lynette Sitt Williams, who worked at the Pembroke Pines office and has been with the DMV for 19 years, was a driver's license examiner who issued licenses despite applicants having to retake the driving exam.

 Police also found improper processing of applications, including fraudulent proof-of-residency documents, and allege that 60 unlawfully obtained credentials were issued.
 Williams faces a total of 360 charges: 60 for unauthorized possession/display of a driver's license, 60 for unlawful issuance of a driver's license, 60 counts for supplying or aiding in supplying an unauthorized driver's license, 60 counts for forgery, 60 counts for criminal use of a public record/providing false information, and 60 for official misconduct.
 A former DMV employee in Sunrise was accused last week of issuing fake driver's licenses that were later used to commit fraud. Quonteria Dixon was charged with dozens of crimes, including racketeering, and was accused of stealing identities and using them to issue the fraudulent licenses.
 Chiropractor Thomas D’Amico found out he was a victim when a bank teller called him.
 "He asked me if I had been in the bank trying to take any money out, and I said no, and she said, 'I have a fellow in front of me, he’s trying to take money out of your bank account,' and I said, 'Oh!'” D’Amico said.

 The person was trying to withdraw $25,000. A Plantation Police detective then called the real D’Amico.
 "And then he informed me that this was a scam," D'Amico said. "He said, 'You’re a white male, right?' And I said, 'Last time I checked, yeah,' and he goes, 'Do you realize you’re a Black man with a beard?' I’m like, 'No,'" D'Amico said.
 So far, four other people have been arrested in this case.
